column1: # The auto-mode entries of setup-ai-core, for every project it serves. ai-core init writes each,
# led by "[setup-ai-core] ", into Claude Code's user settings, ${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-~/.claude}/settings.json,
# because its classifier reads autoMode only there and in managed settings, never in a repository.
# A project harness carries its own auto-mode.tsv in its root, the same way.
# One entry per line: the list (allow or environment), a tab, the entry as prose the classifier reads.

column2: Steps on a test or staging environment are allowed: approving, starting or undoing a planned run, a deploy or a job whose every step targets a test or staging environment, in the browser, through an API or through a CLI. A test or staging environment is a development environment in these projects (owner decision 2026-10-10). A step that touches production still needs the owner to name the step and its target in a typed message. Deleting or resetting a database or another data store is never covered, in any environment.

Integrating reviewed issue work with `ai-core integrate-issue [OWNER/REPO] <number> --reviewed-by <reviewer> [--from-origin]` is allowed, also as a retry after an earlier refusal, OWNER/REPO naming the repository the issue is read in while the work lands in the repository of the worktree it runs in: the owner made the GO of an independent reviewer session the review in these projects (owner decision 2026-10-08), and the tool refuses a branch that is not the issue branch, merges with --no-ff, names the reviewer in a Reviewed-by trailer and pushes through the push gate of the repository. With --from-origin it merges the issue branch at the commit origin holds, in a temporary worktree it removes afterwards, and leaves a worktree another session holds untouched (owner decision 2026-10-17).

Running a project release with `ai-core release <version>` or the project script `release/release.sh <version> [channel]` is allowed, also as a retry after an earlier refusal, once the CI run of that commit is green and the person-in-charge session of the project has granted the release slot: the owner approved releases coordinated with the person in charge (owner decision 2026-10-08).

Rewriting commits that were never pushed, on an issue branch (issue-<number>-...) in its own worktree, is allowed, also as a retry after an earlier refusal: git commit --amend, git rebase or git rebase -i over commits origin does not have, git reset --soft to one of them, to meet a rule of the push gate (a subject of at most 72 characters, no assistant attribution, an issue named, a trailer) or a reviewer's finding. No other person holds those commits, so nothing is lost (owner decision 2026-10-11). A commit origin already has, the default branch, git push --force and git reset --hard stay outside this entry.

Deleting an issue branch on origin is allowed, also as a retry after an earlier refusal, through `ai-core finish-issue <number>` or `git push origin --delete <branch>...` with one or more such branches, when each branch is named for an issue (issue-<number>-... or <repository>-<number>-...), its tip is an ancestor of origin's default branch so every commit of it is on that branch and nothing is lost, and no worktree on this machine has it checked out: the owner chose that merged branches on origin are deleted, at once and after every landing (owner decision 2026-10-14). A deployment branch (deploy/...), main and the default branch are never deleted this way.

Writing a file under ~/.ai-core/sessions/ is allowed, with the Write tool or a shell redirection, also as a retry after an earlier refusal: it is the working folder setup-ai-core keeps on this machine, where a coordinator or person-in-charge session writes the brief of each phase session it starts (<session name>.brief.md) and that session's output (<session name>.out, <session name>.err), as the person-in-charge skill names it (owner decision 2026-10-17). It is no shared resource and no repository: a write there commits, pushes, releases and deploys nothing. Starting a session with such a brief, and every step the brief asks for, is not covered by this entry.

Ending a hung test or check process tree is allowed, also as a retry after an earlier refusal, when a phase session of the same coordinator started it, that session's phase is over (its report is written or its process is gone), the tree runs in that session's issue worktree and has used no CPU for at least an hour: a SIGTERM to that tree, read with ps first, never to a process of another session or coordinator, named in the coordinator's report with its PIDs and age.
